evidence: lib/utils.js:25 same unfiltered '.' split as the writer

lib/utils.js:55-63 legitimate own data keys named 'constructor'/'prototype' (e.g. {constructor:{...}}) go through the same loop; a blanket name denylist breaks them, while an own-property check doesn't

conflicts.what: the natural fix for T2 (reject any 'constructor'/'prototype' segment) also refuses legitimate own data keys with those names that set/getAndCreate should still handle (lib/utils.js:55-63)
filtering the raw segment before the %2E decode (lib/utils.js:54), or refusing '.'/'%' in segments, would break the dotted-key behaviour covered by test/dotted-key.coffee:23-56

fairness_risks: Own data keys named 'constructor' or 'prototype' have no tests (test/manipulate.coffee, test/dotted-key.coffee); a hidden test requiring them to keep working would be fair only if the task says so, because a name denylist is the common upstream-style fix.
%2E dotted keys are a must-keep-working shape (test/dotted-key.coffee:23-56); hidden tests must not refuse them.

src/ vs lib/: if hidden tests run 'grunt test' (GruntFile.coffee:38), a fix made only in lib/ gets overwritten; if they require lib/ directly (test/*.coffee:2), a fix made only in src/ fails. The harness has to pick one and say which.
T4 (getValue returning Object.prototype) is not pollution by itself; requiring getValue to refuse prototype segments goes beyond either advisory and should be stated in the report if tested.

design.why: The only real security fix site is the getAndCreate segment loop (lib/utils.js:53-65). T1 (__proto__) and T2 (constructor.prototype) are closed by one guard there, so they count as ONE group, with T5 as its coupled must-keep value. T3 is a build-artifact duplicate (src compiled to lib), not an independent judgement, and T4 is a read-only route a solver can fairly dismiss. That leaves at most 2 independent security groups, below the 3-5 needed. The best this candidate can offer is a single-group task: T1+T2 as the deepseek-type trap (an incomplete __proto__-only fix) plus T5 as the mimo-type coupled value (keep own 'constructor' keys and %2E keys working). That beats any 3-trap design because T3 and T4 would add build or scope ambiguity, not independent security judgements.
